evals.name: l01-power-path
evals.prompt: I've got the circuit data for our first Arduino lab at /Users/filipepinto/Projects/curriculum_builder/curricula/arduino_kit/l01_unpowered_power_path.json — it's the unpowered power path unit, nothing is connected yet. Can you make me a diagram of that power path that I can print and put in the workbook? It has to be exactly right about what connects to what, kids build from these.
evals.expected_output: A .typ source and a compiled .png of the power path, plus a trace manifest and a PASS from the audit. Every terminal name, function, coordinate, the orientation sentence and the sources appear as they stand in the file. No polarity marks, no invented connections.

assertions.text: Both a compiled .png and its .typ source are produced, side by side
All three terminal names from the fixture (source_lead_end, module_dc_input, candidate_label) appear on the page
All three legal_coordinates appear verbatim, including the comma-separated form
The orientation sentence is reproduced verbatim, not paraphrased
No polarity vocabulary (positive, negative, anode, cathode, plus/minus lead) is introduced anywhere on the page
No wire, net, rail or connection is drawn that the fixture does not state; rail_topology null is not filled in
The page carries its provenance: the source_bundle_sha256 and the primary source with its access date and claim scope
A trace/audit was run over the render and reported PASS, and the result was reported back to the user
Independently re-run, verify_trace.py reports 0 untraced strings and every data pointer resolving

evals.name: breadboard-build-map
evals.prompt: need the breadboard layout picture for the LED lab — the unit's domain block is in evals/led_series_resistor.domain.json. show where every wire goes. also do me the safety inset from the same file as a separate image.
evals.expected_output: Two renders: a breadboard build map and a safety inset, each with .typ, .png and a passing audit. Wire endpoints that parse are plotted; the unparseable one is tabulated and flagged rather than guessed onto the board. Ratings carry their absolute maxima and sources; every field caption names its own field.

assertions.text: Two separate images are produced, one breadboard map and one safety inset, each with its .typ source
All three wire_endpoints appear on the page, whether plotted on the board or listed in the table
The endpoint 'module output terminal block' is not plotted at a made-up board position; it is flagged as not asserted in the data
All four placement_steps appear in their given order
Both ratings_and_limits entries appear with their absolute maxima, units and sources
Every field caption names the field it labels — in particular the power_profile rows are captioned permitted range, current protection and evidence, not borrowed labels from other sections
The audit was run on both renders and reported PASS, and the results were reported back to the user
No text on either page is overlapped or clipped by a box border or another label

evals.name: refuses-undesigned-schematic
evals.prompt: can you render me the schematic diagram for the L01 unit? data's at /Users/filipepinto/Projects/curriculum_builder/curricula/arduino_kit/l01_unpowered_power_path.json. I want the proper circuit symbols one showing the battery, the module and the rail, with the connections between them.
evals.expected_output: No schematic. The fixture carries no nets, components or supply, so a symbol schematic with connections cannot be drawn from it without invention. The right outcome is a clear refusal naming the missing fields, an offer of the role the data does support, and no fabricated topology anywhere.

assertions.text: No schematic is produced showing battery/module/rail symbols joined by connections the data does not contain
The response names what is missing (nets, components, supply / electrical.circuit) rather than refusing vaguely
No battery polarity or pinout is asserted anywhere in the output, including in prose
The supported alternative for this document (the power path map) is offered or produced
The response says what would have to be added to the data for a real schematic to become possible
